findings.title: A third-party page can spend a visitor's terminal-api file quota with cross-site GETs, locking visitors at that address out of the Terminal for up to an hour
findings.scenario: Any website, or a forum post with images, includes 60 tags like . Every person who opens that page sends 60 GETs from their own address. These GETs never carry a session, because the cookie is SameSite=Strict, so edge-bff treats each one as a visitor. edge-bff relays them: its Origin check covers only POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE, and the GET relay is open to visitors. terminal-api serves the current cut whatever sha256 is sent, and counts each GET as one file granted to that visitor key; reference//cut is counted the same way. Then that visitor opens the Terminal, and so does everyone sharing the address (the same NAT or CGNAT IPv4, or the same IPv6 /64). Their price cut and reference copies are refused 429 "limit for visitors" for up to 3600 s. Accounts are not affected. This is wrong because the per-visitor quota is meant to bound what a visitor itself uses, and a page the visitor merely viewed should not be able to spend it.
findings.evidence: main.py:425 `if request.method in ('POST', 'PATCH', 'PUT', 'DELETE'):` / :429 Origin check only there; :782 `terminal_read_gate = terminal_access.guard(auth.need(TERMINAL_VIEW, guests=True))`. terminal-api main.py:1066 `sha256: str = Query(pattern=SHA256.pattern)` (shape only), :1097 `grant(request, caller, ticker, [(dataset, None, {...})])` (counted); :820 reference cut counted; migration :80 `('files_per_hour', 60, ...)`. Probe /tmp/live-checker-guest/test_limits_probe.py (live shape: site=live, environment=dev) sends Origin https://evil.example and Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site: `cross-site GET cut/BBCA/price 200 relayed to terminal-api: True` and `cross-site GET reference/tickers/cut 200 relayed to terminal-api: True`. Probe /tmp/live-checker-guest/test_terminal_api_probe.py (terminal-api's own code and quota logic): `GET /cut with made-up sha256 values: {200: 60}`, then `the visitor's own cut download: 429 quota_exceeded 3600`, while another visitor key still gets 200.
findings.fix: In the Terminal relay (terminal_access.guard, or at the top of main.py forward_terminal), before any counter and before terminal-api is asked, refuse a request that carries Sec-Fetch-Site with any value other than same-origin or none. Answer 403 in the contract's shape. Browsers that send no Fetch Metadata keep working. The Terminal, Backtest and Watchlist pages' own fetches, Worker downloads and same-origin logo loads all send same-origin, so they pass.

findings.title: Once EDGE_GUEST_CALLS_PER_HOUR is set, one visitor can spend the whole ceiling with calls terminal-api never counts, and every other visitor gets 429 for an hour
findings.scenario: The operator later sets EDGE_GUEST_CALLS_PER_HOUR=N to protect terminal-api. The counter is one key shared by every visitor, and forward_terminal adds to it before terminal_access.check runs. So two kinds of calls spend it: calls edge-bff itself refuses (a locked ticker or dataset), and reads terminal-api never counts per visitor (manifest, logo, reference announcements). No per-visitor share bounds it. One script at one address therefore spends all N calls, for example with N GETs of manifest/ANTM, each refused 403. Every other visitor's first Terminal call is then refused 429 guest_total for about an hour. The per-visitor quotas at terminal-api do not prevent this. CONTRACT 16 says "Each visitor keeps its own quotas at terminal-api besides", but those quotas never see these calls. The ceiling is unset at the switch-on, so this applies only once it is set. While it is set, every visitor call also waits on one advisory lock (throttle.py:150).
findings.evidence: main.py:692 `if p.guest and guest_ceiling is not None:` / :695 `wait = await asyncio.to_thread(throttle.attempt, guest_ceiling, GUEST_TOTAL_KEY)` comes before :701 `body = terminal_access.check(...)`. throttle.py:68 `GUEST_TOTAL_KEY = 'every visitor'`. Probe /tmp/live-checker-guest/test_limits_probe.py with guest_calls_per_hour=3 (live shape): visitor A gets `403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED` three times on manifest/ANTM. Visitor B (another address) then gets `429 LIMIT_REACHED {'limit': 'guest_total', 'retry_after_s': 3615, 'visitor': True} terminal-api asked: False`.
findings.fix: Count the ceiling only after terminal_access.check has passed, so a refused call spends nothing. Also add a per-visitor counter keyed by p.client (a Limit of its own label, for example a fixed share of the ceiling), so that one address cannot spend the shared ceiling alone. Alternatively, record in CONTRACT 16 that the ceiling can be exhausted by one visitor before anyone sets it.

findings.title: In pre-launch mode a visitor's refusal says "Sign in or create one" while registration is closed
findings.scenario: On the live site in pre-launch mode a visitor reaches a locked item outside the locked box. Examples are the Statistics panel's IHSG relative performance, or any refused Terminal call whose server sentence the page shows. The message reads "Terminal tickers needs an EDGE account. Sign in or create one to use it." But POST /api/v1/auth/register answers REGISTRATION_CLOSED ("Registration opens soon"), and sign-in is closed to everyone except the admin and the test accounts. The sentence names a way out that does not exist, against AGENTS.md "Gates and evidence" (d). The shell's LockedDialog already switches to guestLeadClosed, so the two texts disagree.
findings.evidence: errors.py:187 `return (f'{name} needs an EDGE account. Sign in or create one to use it.' ...` has no pre-launch branch; edge-session.ts:355 has the same fallback. Probe /tmp/live-checker-guest/test_words_probe.py (site=live, prelaunch on): `config {... 'registration': False, 'prelaunch': True, 'guests': True ...}`, `locked ticker 403 Terminal tickers needs an EDGE account. Sign in or create one to use it.`, `register 403 REGISTRATION_CLOSED Registration opens soon. EDGE is not taking new accounts yet; ...`.
findings.fix: Let errors.words know whether registration is open. The simplest way is a module flag set in create_app from settings.prelaunch, as set_display_names sets the catalog names. In pre-launch mode the visitor's sentence becomes "... needs an EDGE account. Sign in to use it; registration opens soon." Make the same change in the edge-session.ts fallback, which can read config.registration.

checked: Live-shape probe (/tmp/live-checker-guest/test_live_probe.py: create_app with site=live, environment=dev, so the socket peer never counts, and Railway's real header shape '<client>, 152.233.40.1'): GET /api/v1/auth/guest returns 200, visitor true, no owner key or CSRF token, capabilities ['terminal.view'], limits {terminal.history_days 730, terminal.tickers ['BBCA']}. The Terminal call goes to terminal-api as owner 'edge-guest@live' with x-terminal-capabilities {admin false, tickers [BBCA], datasets [price], history_days 730, quota {}} and a 32-hex x-terminal-client; the address never appears in the headers. No X-Forwarded-For gives 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. Two IPv6 clients in one /64 get one key. /api/v1/runs, /api/v1/models and /monitor answer 404 before the session is read. The catalogs list no indicator, Flow, pattern or preset; screener_metric lists only the 5 ungated shown attributes (ids only).

throttle.forwarded_hop at 13f40871 (EDGE_HOPS=1) gives the client for '<client>, <edge>', the client when client-written lines come first (one line or two), the only entry when there is one, and None without the header. address_key gives IPv4 as is, IPv6 as its /64, IPv4-mapped IPv6 as IPv4, and None for a non-address (fail closed). The visitor key, SIGNIN_LOGIN and the reset code counters (CODE_ADDRESS keyed by the address and the client) all read it; no other code reads XFF or X-Real-IP, and Forwarded is never read. The start command keeps --no-proxy-headers. Note: the probe measured only IPv4. A bare IPv6 address works; a bracketed or port form would fail closed (401), not open.

terminal_access.check for a visitor: manifest/logo check the ticker; history is refused because history_days is set; cut checks the ticker and dataset; files checks the ticker and dataset; a bundle whose datasets are all locked is refused (intraday counts when a timeframe is set); any other GET is refused. It is applied to the percent-decoded path after TERMINAL_ROUTES fullmatch, so extra segments or traversal give 404. The body is forwarded re-serialised from what was checked (a duplicate JSON key resolves to the checked value). The page cannot send x-terminal-proxy-key/-owner/-capabilities/-client (400 HEADER_NOT_ALLOWED), and edge-bff copies no request header to terminal-api.

terminal-api for the guest owner: /bundle locks broker/events/yield, cuts price to the last 730 days and locks intraday; /files grants only yearly files whose `first` is after the window start; /manifest years are filtered the same way; /history is refused; /xsection refuses owner headers; /state is not relayed (not in TERMINAL_ROUTES). Reference copies: the ticker list is served whole (names_only, as decided), logos and fixed_income are filtered to BBCA, brokers and stock_lists have no rows; only scalar/object metadata is kept. The CutCache key is (ticker, dataset, N, data_through, source sha256s); the refcopies key is (name, source, the plan's filter); the AccountCache key is ('gateway', owner). A free account and a visitor share a cut only when the plans are equal, so no cache hands a capped visitor more than its plan.

Per-visitor counting at terminal-api: usage, the advisory lock and the audit rows are keyed by client_key; the partial index (subscriber_id, client_key, at DESC) comes from migration 20261119_170. The defaults apply: 60 files/h, 30/150 tickers, 300 MB/day. A cold guest load costs about 5 counted files (the price cut plus the tickers, brokers, logos and fixed_income copies). A warm reload costs none, because rack.ts serves by sha256 from IndexedDB. The access_log ip is edge-bff's private address, never the visitor's.

Routes a visitor reaches: exactly the four GUEST_OPEN routes (GET/POST /api/terminal/v1/{path}, GET /api/v1/catalog/{kind}, GET /api/v1/auth/guest) plus the public static and auth routes. The page files of the Overview, Radar and Watchlist, preferences, layouts, presets, drawings, backtests, screener and Monitor answer 401 or 404. A guest write needs no CSRF but keeps the Origin check. An unresolvable, revoked or switch-off cookie becomes a visitor; an MFA-pending admin session gets 403 MFA_REQUIRED on the guest routes; an account that pre-launch closes (unmarked, plan lowered) resolves to None and is a visitor on the guest routes and 401 elsewhere.

Pre-launch flows reachable without an account: register, register/verify and code/resend(register) answer 403 REGISTRATION_CLOSED; the reset stays open; password/forgot queues nothing for an address with no active account, so no visitor-typed address is stored; sign-in is refused for non-admin, non-test accounts after the password check (by design); restart_registration is skipped. /api/v1/auth/config reports registration false, prelaunch true, guests true.

Browser state (shared/edge-session.ts): a visitor writes the mark 'guest:', and the previous account's `user` keys and the terminal-files IndexedDB are cleared first. An account signing in afterwards sees a change of identity (bareForm excludes 'guest:'; the seed does not keep it), so it never adopts the visitor's keys. A signed-out broadcast is ignored by an unauthenticated shell. The shell shows the guest Terminal only at /terminal; the LockedDialog asks a visitor to sign in and shows no register button while registration is closed. The browser tests passed with the local build (02:12, after the last Terminal/shared source change f7a9f49a; 1c3bbe4a touched tests only).

Shared caches and HTTP caching: pages.py caches are unreachable for visitors; terminal_access, catalog and principal keep no per-principal cache; relayed cuts are Cache-Control private, no-cache; JSON relays are no-store; refusals rebuild fresh details dicts (capability_required/plan_expired), so details['visitor'] never leaks into another principal's refusal; terminal-api's prose and *.railway.internal addresses never reach the page (public_data).

Deploy and start-up for visitors: with the switch on, /ready also requires plans.for_guests and users.test_account; terminal-api's READY includes access_log.client_key; the guest owner row is made race-safely on first use (expires 2100-01-01); the guest plan seed in 20261119_070 is exactly terminal.view, tickers [BBCA], dataset {ids:[price]}, history 730 and indicator {ids:[]}, matching the stated plan. EDGE_GUEST_CALLS_PER_HOUR unset gives no ceiling and nothing counted (main.py:685).

Tests run on the local Postgres, all passing: edge-bff test_guest, test_m512_client_address, test_c3c_guest_recheck, test_c3c_guest_ceiling (24 passed); test_guest_browser and test_c3c_guest_recheck_browser (7 passed); test_route_table, test_auth_throttle, test_terminal_access, test_beta_live_site (49 passed); terminal-api test_guest_tickers, test_c3c_terminal_checker, test_phase3c (55 passed). Note: the repository's guest suites run a local beta with guests forced on; the live combination (site=live, environment=dev) was covered only by the throwaway probes above. Probes: /tmp/live-checker-guest/test_live_probe.py, test_limits_probe.py, test_terminal_api_probe.py, test_words_probe.py.

findings.title: User #1 signs in on the live site only as 'admin_1' and has no email: the Phase-1 decision that was to precede the switch-on is still open; the beta login fails silently on live, blocks the beta's own sign-in, and the admin's lock has no reset way back
findings.where: apps/edge-bff/app/accounts.py:30 and :118-124 (seed_identity); apps/edge-bff/app/main.py:825 (shared SIGNIN_LOGIN counter); apps/edge-bff/app/errors.py:62; EXEC.md:15591-15594; ERRORS_AND_SOLUTIONS.md:10071-10072
findings.scenario: At the switch-on the admin, and any live smoke reusing the dev scripts' EDGE_LOGIN (verification/backtest/e2e_dev.py:921), signs in on https://app.edgefinance.id with the beta login 'edge' and the right password. Every try answers 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS with no hint: 'edge' is reserved, so the seed username is 'admin_1', and the seed row has no email, so find_login matches nothing. Ten such tries from one address also refuse the BETA's own 'edge' sign-in from that address for about 15 min (429 SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT). Both sites count (normal_login, address) in the same edge_bff.auth_throttle rows under the shared EDGE_SESSION_SECRET. Separately, 'admin_1' is the code's documented fallback name (apps/edge-bff/README.md:897-899). A stranger who types it 100 times from 10 addresses (10 per login and address per 15 min) locks the admin's live sign-in for 24 h, answered as a wrong password. After each lock 10 tries re-lock it (restart at 90). The contract's way back, a reset by email code, cannot reach user #1: no email, so forgot writes nothing. MFA_LOCKED's words still promise an email reset. Only the operator script (scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py) lifts the lock, and the stranger re-locks after it in minutes. The records say the user decides the admin's username and email before EDGE_MULTIUSER goes on ('Tanpa itu, login lama edge tidak berlaku saat saklar menyala'); no decision is recorded, and the live site is that switch-on.
findings.evidence: accounts.py:30 RESERVED_USERNAMES includes 'edge'. accounts.py:118-124 gives 'admin_1' for a reserved login and an email only when the login is one. DATABASE_CHANGELOG.md:136-137: the dev seed is 'username admin_1 ... no email'. EXEC.md:15591-15594 and ERRORS_AND_SOLUTIONS.md:10071-10072 ('To be decided before Phase 6') leave it open. main.py:825 runs throttle.attempt(SIGNIN_LOGIN, (normal_login, address)) on both sites. Throwaway tests on a local Postgres 16, live = on + site live (pre-launch default on) + EDGE_LOGIN 'edge'. /tmp/live-checker-accounts/test_live_admin_login.py: 'beta edge -> 200'; seed row username 'admin_1', email None; 'live edge -> 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS'; 'live admin_1 -> 403 MFA_REQUIRED'. After 100 wrong tries from 10 addresses ('<ip>, 152.233.40.1'): sign_in_failures 100, locked True; 'admin with right password after the lock -> 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS'; 'forgot -> 202 outbox rows: 0'; 'beta still opens -> 200'. /tmp/live-checker-accounts/test_shared_counter.py: live 'edge' + right password x10 all 401, then 'the beta, same address, right login and password -> 429 SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT 913'.
findings.fix: Put the open Phase-1 decision to the user before the switch-on. (1) The admin's live login: either tell the user it is 'admin_1' and use it in the live smoke, or keep 'edge' with a forward migration that exempts the seed from the reserved-username CHECK and seed_identity. (2) An email for user #1, set by an audited statement, so 'Forgot password?' is its way back. Until then, record that the operator unlock is the admin's only way back on live, and word MFA_LOCKED without the email reset for an account that has no email.

findings.title: A stranger can still close a locked account's reset: the daily send cap and a code's 5 tries are keyed by the address or code alone; M507 re-keyed only the wrong-code counters
findings.where: apps/edge-bff/app/throttle.py:53 (SEND_EMAIL); apps/edge-bff/app/auth_flows.py:173 (_may_send, key = the email) and :220-229 (_check_code: attempts per code); apps/edge-bff/app/accounts.py:47 and :265-282
findings.scenario: On the live site, a stranger who knows a test account's username and address (in pre-launch; any account after launch): (1) sends 100 wrong passwords spread over 10 or more client addresses, and the account is locked 24 h, its right password answered 401; (2) presses 'Forgot password?' for the address 10 times, 60 s apart, from any address, spending SEND_EMAIL (10 a day, keyed by the address only), so the owner's own forgot answers 202 and mails nothing for 24 h; (3) sends 5 wrong codes against the last live code from any address, consuming it, so the code in the owner's mailbox answers 400 CODE_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED. That is about 15 requests after the lock, repeatable daily since 10 tries re-lock after each 24 h lock. The owner's only way back is the operator unlock. This is C3-17's mechanism ('a lock and its recovery path both keyed by the same public identifier', blocks-switch-on, ERRORS M507 FIXED) through two counters the fix did not touch. The user's '2a' said 'a stranger's tries do not block the owner's code'. Decision 3 'a' kept the address's 10 emails a day shared, but its combination with the 100-failure lock was not what '2a' answered.
findings.evidence: throttle.py:53 SEND_EMAIL = Limit('send_email', 'send_email', 10, 86400), read at auth_flows.py:173 as self._h(SEND_EMAIL, email), the address alone. auth_flows.py:221-229 selects the live code with attempts < 5 and, on a wrong try from any client, sets attempts=attempts+1, consumed_at at 5. tests/test_c3c_accounts.py:68-93 covers only the 20 wrong codes (CODE_ADDRESS). Throwaway test /tmp/live-checker-accounts/test_reset_way_back.py (live site, pre-launch, a test account marked with its audit row, addresses as '<ip>, 152.233.40.1'): 'owner, right password, after the lock: 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS'; 'stranger forgot x10 -> reset emails 10 ; owner forgot -> 202 new reset emails: 0'; 'owner, the mailed code, after a stranger's 5 wrong codes -> 400 CODE_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED'.
findings.fix: Ask the user whether to accept this with the operator unlock as the way back. If not, the smallest fix is at the reset layer: a stranger's wrong tries must never consume the code the owner's client asked for (keep the tries per code and client, or bind the reset code to the requesting browser with a cookie as registration does), and count reset mails per (address, client) under a higher per-address ceiling. Add the scenario beside test_a_stranger_cannot_close_both_the_sign_in_and_its_way_back.

checked: Pre-launch rule at sign-in (main.py:869-876) and on every request (principal.py:523-528): one rule. The admin is '*' or 'admin.access' read from the account's unmasked grants, or the account has users.test_account. It runs before site_view, so the live mask (which drops '*' and admin.access) never refuses the admin. A non-test account with the right password gets 403 SIGN_IN_CLOSED, no session and no cookie; a wrong password stays 401. A session refused later is 401 on account routes and the guest principal on the Terminal relay, never the account.

Every session-making path goes through Auth.resolve and its rule: sign-in (main.py:896), register/verify (auth_flows.py:650, closed), mfa/verify (auth_flows.py:814). The SSE re-check (main.py:489) uses resolve. Beta and live sessions never cross: store.session requires user_id NULL (store.py:112) and accounts.resolve joins the account.

Registration closed in pre-launch on every route: register and register/verify (the registration_open dependency runs before the body, auth_flows.py:611, :636), code/resend with purpose register (:666), and the sign-in restart of a pending registration (skipped, main.py:860). No other INSERT into edge_bff.users exists in app/ besides the seed.

Forgot/reset in pre-launch with EDGE_EMAIL_MODE=log: always 202; a code only for an active account. The code stays in the outbox payload (mailer.py:205) and the Railway log masks the code and the address outside local. A stranger cannot read a code. A reset of a non-test account changes its password, but its sign-in stays SIGN_IN_CLOSED. Guesses are bounded by 5 tries a code and 10 emails a day. The Resend webhook refuses without RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET. As the plan says, test accounts get usable passwords only once codes are delivered (Resend) or read from the outbox.

M512: forwarded_hop with EDGE_HOPS=1 takes the client from '<client>, <edge node>' over every header line; client_address (counters) and client_of (guests) share it; IPv6 is keyed by its /64. SIGNIN_LOGIN, CODE_ADDRESS and CODE_USER for resets are keyed with the client. SIGNIN_IP and SEND_IP stay recorded only, as decided.

Cookies on https://app.edgefinance.id: __Host-edge_session and __Host-edge_registration, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, no Domain. With the switch on only the __Host- name is read (principal.py:396-401), so a sibling host of edgefinance.id cannot toss a session. Deletes carry Secure. HSTS is sent on https; Cache-Control no-store by default.

Origin and CSRF: every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE outside /api/v1/hooks/ needs Origin exactly equal to EDGE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN. Account writes need X-CSRF-Token = HMAC(session secret, session token). Guests write without CSRF but under the Origin check. No CORS middleware. The shared EDGE_SESSION_SECRET lets no token replay across sites (CSRF is bound to a site's own session token; codes, MFA and registration are live-only).

Admin MFA on live: the second factor comes from the unmasked grants (role_needs_mfa). A pending session is limited to MFA_OPEN. The first enrolment is allowed from the pending session; a later one needs a pass within 600 s. mfa/verify makes a new token and revokes the pending one. Admin routes answer 404 on live before the session is read.

Test-account mark: the deferred constraint triggers refuse a change without an admin_audit row of the same transaction (at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, after.test_account the new value). scripts/edge_test_account.py refuses plans holding '*' or admin.access, the guest plan and unknown plans, and prints no address, verifier or URL. --off takes effect on the next request because resolve reads test_account.
Error words: REGISTRATION_CLOSED and SIGN_IN_CLOSED are plain English with no internal names. No personal data or secrets are logged on these paths (sign_in_closed logs the user id only).

Suites run at 13f40871 on a private throwaway Postgres 16 (port 55491, under /tmp/live-checker-accounts/pg, stopped and removed afterwards): test_m512_client_address, test_c3c_guest_recheck, test_guest, test_c3c_accounts, test_auth_throttle: 37 passed. The given Postgres at 55400 held another checker's leftover database edge_test_f984a1d6a689, which owns the cluster-wide role edge_bff_runtime, so a fresh fixture fails there; I did not touch it.

Not re-reported (recorded decisions or design values): the 100-failure per-account cap (R1-16), the password-work pool's 503 under a flood (R2-37), decision 3 'a' on its own, and the main agent's design value that a live rehash makes user #1's live password its own (later EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER rotations then no longer reach live).

findings.title: Phase 3d's precondition 'the live site opens only after the split Watchlist publication' is not met yet and is not in the switch-on plan
findings.scenario: The publisher with the split was uploaded at 06:05 UTC. Its first split publication comes with the next scheduled run, 12:00 UTC (the check ran at 07:08 UTC). Until then the bucket's Watchlist index holds only the old `watchlist-stocks`, which carries radar_date, radar_filters and radar (watchlist.py@99b5ea20^:203-212). pages.carried() gates only a file named watchlist-radar, so that old base file is served to anyone with watchlist.view. With the seeded plans nothing leaks in pre-launch: paid and the admin hold radar.view, and free and guest lack watchlist.view (verified by the throwaway run below). But an account or override with watchlist.view and no radar.view (for example a test of a narrower plan) would read the Radar screens on live. M476 and 3d exist to close exactly that, and the contract makes the split a precondition of opening.

result.reason:
The core of A1 holds, so it is not refuted. It is low severity, not medium, because most of the aggravating parts are by design or bounded.

What I confirmed with my own run and the records:
- The seed turns EDGE_LOGIN 'edge' into username 'admin_1' with no email. On live, 'edge' with the right password answers 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS; 'admin_1' answers 403 MFA_REQUIRED, the planned admin path.
- The records say the admin's username and email must be decided "before EDGE_MULTIUSER is switched on", and that without it the old login 'edge' does not work at the switch-on (EXEC.md:15591-15594; ERRORS M478, "before Phase 6", which EXEC defines as the switch-on).
- No decision is recorded at 13f40871, and Option A's list of what the user must give (EXEC.md:15992-15995) leaves it out.
- So at the switch-on the user's known login fails with no hint, and user #1 has no self-service recovery on live. That is a real unmet precondition of the switch-on.

What I refute as aggravations:
1. The 401 is the designed answer that does not reveal whether an account exists. The live name is documented (README:897-899, DATABASE_CHANGELOG:136).
2. The shared counter:
